about.title: Three seats, one product
about.lead: Developer, test automation engineer, scrum master. The same product seen from three angles, which turns out to be the useful part.
intro: I build web applications end to end and then I try very hard to break them. Ten of those years have been spent moving between three seats — writing the feature, automating the tests that keep it honest, and facilitating the team that ships it.

Day to day that means JavaScript and TypeScript on React front ends, Python and Java on the back, and a C# service when the platform calls for it. I care most about the part people rarely see: a suite that fails for the right reason, a component that stays readable a year later, an interface that works with a keyboard.
Outside work I run models locally with Ollama and pair with Claude on side projects, mostly to understand where AI actually earns its place in a workflow and where it just adds noise.

journey.title: Where I have worked
journey.lead: Ten years, three job titles, one consistent interest: making it work and proving that it does.

entries.summary: Feature work across a React and TypeScript front end with Node and Java services behind it.
highlights: Rebuilt a legacy view as composable React components with CSS Modules, cutting render cost on mobile.
Introduced Percy visual regression so design changes stop arriving as surprises.
Mentor two junior developers through code review and pairing.

entries.summary: Facilitated two delivery teams while staying hands-on in the codebase roughly half the week.
highlights: Ran refinement, retros and planning for teams of six to nine people.
Cut lead time by making the definition of done include automated coverage.
Kept writing code — a scrum master who cannot read the backlog technically is a messenger.

entries.summary: Owned the automated test estate: unit, integration, end to end and visual.
highlights: Migrated a brittle TestCafe suite to Playwright, taking runtime from 40 to 11 minutes.
Built pytest service tests that run against ephemeral environments in CI.
Made flaky tests a tracked defect class rather than something people re-ran.

entries.summary: Built and maintained internal web tools on a MERN stack.
highlights: Shipped the first React rewrite of an internal admin tool.
Wrote the team's first Jest tests and the habit stuck.

entries.summary: Two years of fullstack training with internship placements, from databases to deployment.
highlights: Java and JavaScript foundations, relational databases, agile methodology.

approach.title: How I work
approach.lead: Five things I will bring to your team on day one, whichever of the three seats you put me in.

principles.title: Tests are a design tool
principles.body: If a component is hard to test it is usually badly shaped. I write the test to find that out early, not to satisfy a coverage gate.

principles.title: Small surfaces, clear seams
principles.body: One reason to change per module, dependencies pointing at interfaces rather than implementations. This page is built that way — the project list does not know GitHub exists.

principles.title: Accessible by default
principles.body: Keyboard paths, focus order, contrast and reduced motion are part of done. Automated axe checks catch the obvious; I check the rest by hand.

principles.title: Facilitation is engineering work
principles.body: Three years as scrum master taught me that most delivery problems are unclear scope, not slow typing. I still run refinement I am invited to.

principles.title: AI with a measurement attached
principles.body: I use Claude and local models daily, and I treat their output like any contribution — reviewed, tested, and rejected when it is wrong.

exploring.title: What I am learning next
exploring.lead: I would rather show you the edge of what I know than pretend it is not there. These are the six things currently taking up my evenings.

topics.title: Mobile applications
topics.why: I know the web deeply. I want the same fluency on a device — React Native first, then enough native to know when the abstraction leaks.

topics.title: Retrieval augmented generation
topics.why: Chunking, embeddings and ranking are where most RAG systems quietly fail. I want to build one properly instead of gluing a vector store to a prompt.

topics.title: Evaluation harnesses
topics.why: Test automation instincts applied to models. If I cannot measure a change in output quality, I have not really changed anything.

topics.title: Local and private AI
topics.why: Ollama on my own hardware, small models fine-tuned for narrow jobs, no data leaving the machine. Useful and genuinely fun.

topics.title: AI, past the API call
topics.why: Enough of the underlying mechanics — tokenisation, context, tool use — to reason about limits rather than guess at them.

topics.title: Robotics
topics.why: Software that moves something physical has a feedback loop nothing else does. Starting with microcontrollers and sensors.
